result: H3K36me3 is reduced in both H3-G34V and H3-G34R mutants, while H3K36me2 accumulates in both strains.
evaluation: Claims C34, C52, C55, and C65 are supported by western blot data in Figure 1C showing marked reduction in H3K36me3 in both G34V and G34R mutants compared to wild-type, with accumulation of H3K36me2. The antibody recognition controls (C53, C54) provide additional validation of the measurements.

result: H3-G34R but not H3-G34V mutants show defective H3K36 acetylation.
evaluation: Claims C35, C62, C63, and C64 are supported by mass spectrometry data (Figure 1D) and in vitro acetylation assays (Figure 1F) showing that H3K36ac is greatly reduced in H3-G34R but unaffected in H3-G34V cells. This represents a key phenotypic difference between the two glioma-associated mutations.

result: Gcn5 is the major H3K36 acetyltransferase in fission yeast, and its activity is specifically lost at K36 on G34R H3 in vitro.
evaluation: Claims C68-C71 and C187-C188 are supported by genetic data (Figure 1E) showing gcn5Δ cells have low H3K36ac, and in vitro acetylation assays (Figure 1F) demonstrating that Gcn5 acetylates K36 on WT H3 but activity is strongly reduced on G34R H3 and slowed on G34V H3. The specificity for K36 while other sites remain unaffected strengthens the conclusion.

result: H3-G34R and set2Δ cells are sensitive to multiple forms of replicative stress (HU, MMS, CPT), while H3-G34V cells are not.
evaluation: Claims C76-C83 are supported by serial dilution growth assays (Figure 2A) showing that H3-G34R and set2Δ cells are sensitive to hydroxyurea, methyl methanesulfonate, and camptothecin, whereas H3-G34V cells show no sensitivity to these agents. This demonstrates distinct DNA damage response profiles between G34R and G34V mutants.

result: H3-G34V but not H3-G34R mutants are sensitive to γ-irradiation and IR mimetics.
evaluation: Claims C87-C90 are supported by γ-irradiation viability assays (Figure 2B) and serial dilution assays with bleomycin and zeocin (Figure 2C) showing that H3-G34V and set2Δ cells are sensitive to IR and IR mimetics, while H3-G34R cells are not. This represents another key phenotypic distinction between the two glioma mutations.

result: H3-G34V cells are proficient for homologous recombination while H3-G34R cells are defective for HR.
evaluation: Claims C92-C97 are supported by HR efficiency assays (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) and epistasis analysis with rad51Δ (Figure 2D). The epistasis data showing that rad51Δ H3-G34V double mutants are more sensitive than either single mutant, while rad51Δ H3-G34R double mutants are no more sensitive than rad51Δ alone, provides strong genetic evidence for HR proficiency in G34V and deficiency in G34R.

result: H3-G34R cells exhibit elevated chromosome loss and missegregation, while H3-G34V cells show genomic stability similar to wild-type.
evaluation: Claims C100-C103 and C105 are supported by minichromosome loss assays (Figure 2E) showing H3-G34R cells lose Ch16 at 4.3% frequency compared to 1.2% for WT and 2.2% for G34V, and chromosome missegregation assays (Figure 2F) showing 7.4% lagging chromosomes in G34R versus 0.5% in both WT and G34V. This demonstrates distinct genomic stability profiles.

result: H3K36me3 is specifically reduced in H3-G34K, G34R, and G34V mutants, but not in G34W, G34M, or G34Q mutants, while H3K36me2 is elevated in all G34 mutants.
evaluation: Claims C106-C108 are supported by western blot analysis (Figure 3C) of a panel of G34 mutants showing that only mutations introducing basic charges (K, R) or valine reduce H3K36me3, while bulky uncharged (W, M) or negatively charged (Q) substitutions do not. The elevation of H3K36me2 in all mutants (accounting for antibody recognition differences) suggests a defect in the di- to tri-methylation transition.

result: Among H3-G34 mutants, only G34R is sensitive to hydroxyurea, while both G34R and G34K (basic substitutions) are sensitive to MMS and CPT, but G34W, G34M, and G34Q are not.
evaluation: Claims C109-C112 are supported by serial dilution assays (Figure 3D) showing distinct DNA damage sensitivity patterns. The observation that alkylation sensitivity correlates with basic charge rather than size of substitution (C112) is a reasonable inference from the data, though the mechanism remains unclear.

result: H3-G34K and H3-G34V mutants are sensitive to γ-IR and IR mimetics, with G34K showing greater sensitivity than G34V or set2Δ, while G34R, G34M, G34W, and G34Q are not sensitive.
evaluation: Claims C113-C116 are supported by serial dilution assays with bleomycin and zeocin (Figure 3E) and γ-irradiation viability assays (Figure 3F). The data clearly show that G34K and G34V share IR sensitivity, distinguishing them from G34R, and that G34K is more sensitive than either set2Δ or G34V.

result: H3-G34K and H3-G34R mutants exhibit elevated chromosome missegregation, but only G34R is defective for HR, as demonstrated by epistasis analysis with rad51Δ.
evaluation: Claims C120-C121, C123-C125, and C128 are supported by chromosome missegregation assays (Figure 3G) showing elevated lagging chromosomes in G34K (7.4%) and G34R (5.9%) but not other mutants, and epistasis analysis (Figure 3H-I) showing that G34K rad51Δ double mutants are more sensitive than either single mutant while G34R rad51Δ are not. This demonstrates that chromosome missegregation can occur independently of HR defects.

result: RNA-seq analysis reveals distinct transcriptional profiles for H3-G34R, G34K, and G34V mutants, with differential regulation of subtelomeric (ST) domains: repression in G34R, slight repression in G34K, upregulation in set2Δ, and WT-like profile in G34V.
evaluation: Claims C131-C137 are supported by RNA-seq data (Figure 4A-B, Supplementary file 4) showing that set2Δ has the most differentially expressed genes (478 total), while G34 mutants show fewer changes (160 for G34R, 223 for G34K, 183 for G34V) with only 44 genes misregulated in all three G34 mutants. The distinct ST domain transcriptional profiles are clearly shown in Manhattan plots and validated by RT-PCR.

result: Genes downregulated in both G34R and G34K strains are preferentially located in ST domains, and this downregulation is mirrored in cells lacking the H3K36 acetyltransferases Gcn5 and Mst2.
evaluation: Claims C138-C142 are supported by RNA-seq analysis showing 16/31 downregulated genes in both G34R and G34K are in ST domains versus only 2/29 upregulated genes, and by data showing that gcn5Δmst2Δ cells also show ST domain repression (Figure 4D-E). This links H3K36 acetylation to ST domain transcriptional regulation.

result: H3-G34R cells show elevated subtelomeric 'knob' formation and accumulation of Sgo2 at ST domains, correlating with enhanced silencing; this is mirrored in gcn5Δmst2Δ cells.
evaluation: Claims C148-C149, C151-C153, and C158 are supported by 3D-SIM microscopy showing increased knobs in G34R but not G34V cells (Figure 5A-B), and ChIP data showing Sgo2-FLAG enrichment at ST domains in G34R compared to G34V or WT (Figure 5C) and in gcn5Δmst2Δ cells (Figure 5D). The correlation between Sgo2 accumulation, knob formation, and ST silencing is well-supported.

result: Sgo2 accumulation at centromeres in mitosis is unaffected by H3-G34R mutation, but Sgo2 is preferentially enriched at ST domains even in mitotically arrested G34R cells, suggesting perturbed cell cycle regulation of Sgo2 localization.
evaluation: Claims C155-C157 are supported by ChIP data (Figure 5E-F) showing that Sgo2 levels at centromeres are similar between G34R and WT in mitotic cells, but Sgo2 is enriched at ST domains in G34R even during mitotic arrest. The inference about perturbed cell cycle regulation (C157) is reasonable given the data, though the mechanism remains unclear.

result: H3-G34K cells show elevated Sgo2 at ST domains, consistent with the pattern seen in G34R and H3K36ac-deficient cells.
evaluation: Claim C159 is supported by ChIP data (Figure 5G) showing Sgo2-FLAG enrichment at ST domains in G34K cells. This extends the correlation between basic substitutions at G34, reduced H3K36ac, ST domain silencing, and Sgo2 accumulation.

result: Co-expression of wild-type H3 with G34R, G34V, or G34K mutants does not affect global H3K36me3 or H3K36me2 levels, and loss of H3K36ac is restricted to the G34R mutant protein.
evaluation: Claims C160-C164 are supported by western blot data (Figure 6A) showing no change in H3K36me3 or H3K36me2 in mixed copy strains, and mass spectrometry data (Figure 6B) showing K36ac is present on WT H3 but absent on G34R H3 in mixed copy strains. This demonstrates that K36 methylation and acetylation effects are cis-acting on the mutant histone tail.

result: Most DNA damage sensitivities and chromosome missegregation are rescued in mixed copy strains, but H3-G34R (3xH3) retains dominant HU sensitivity.
evaluation: Claims C165-C167 are supported by serial dilution assays (Figure 6C-D) showing that mixed copy G34K and G34V strains grow like WT on bleomycin and zeocin, but G34R (3xH3) retains HU sensitivity, and chromosome missegregation assays (Figure 6E) showing no increased lagging chromosomes in mixed copy G34K or G34R strains. This demonstrates that most phenotypes are recessive but HU sensitivity in G34R is dominant.

result: H3-G34R mixed copy strains show a significant reduction in HR efficiency compared to wild-type.
evaluation: Claim C168 is supported by HR assay data (Figure 6F) showing reduced efficiency in G34R (3xH3) strains. This demonstrates that HR defects in G34R show partial dominance, consistent with the dominant HU sensitivity.

result: The number of differentially expressed genes is reduced in mixed copy strains compared to sole copy strains, but ST domain repression is maintained in G34R and G34K mixed copy strains, demonstrating dominant transcriptional effects.
evaluation: Claims C169-C177 are supported by RNA-seq data showing fewer differentially expressed genes in mixed copy strains (54 for G34R [3xH3] vs 160 for sole copy G34R), but Manhattan plots (Figure 6G) and RT-PCR (Figure 6H) show ST domain repression is maintained in mixed copy G34R and G34K strains. The enrichment of ST domain genes among repressed genes (10/30 for G34R, 25/69 for G34K) versus activated genes (1/24, 7/73) supports dominant ST silencing.

result: The sensitivity of H3-G34R cells to replicative stress cannot be attributed to reduction in H3K36me3 but may be due to loss of H3K36ac.
evaluation: Claim C84 is supported by the observation that both G34R and G34V have reduced H3K36me3 (C55, C65) but only G34R shows replicative stress sensitivity (C76-C83) and only G34R has reduced H3K36ac (C62-C64). The inference that H3K36ac loss may cause replicative stress sensitivity is reasonable, though causality is not definitively established.

result: All three mutants (G34R, G34V, G34K) with reduced K36me3 show enhanced DNA damage sensitivity, suggesting K36me3 plays a critical role in genome protection, but sensitivity to specific DNA-damaging agents is influenced by additional factors.
evaluation: Claims C117-C119 are supported by the observation that G34R, G34V, and G34K all have reduced K36me3 (C106) and all show some form of DNA damage sensitivity (though to different agents), while mutants without K36me3 reduction (G34W, G34M, G34Q) show no DNA damage sensitivity. The inference that additional factors influence specific sensitivities is reasonable given the non-overlapping damage sensitivity profiles.

result: The mechanism of reduced H3K36me3 in G34V/R mutants remains unclear; Set2 association with chromatin is unchanged, and loss of the demethylase Epe1 does not affect K36 methylation levels.
evaluation: Claims C57-C60 present speculative hypotheses (C57, C58) about defective Set2 trimethylation or heightened demethylase activity, but the experimental tests (ChIP for Set2, C59; deletion of epe1, C60) do not support either mechanism. The claims acknowledge uncertainty but do not provide a definitive mechanism for the K36me3 reduction.

result: The HR defect in G34R cells may be linked to loss of H3K36ac, but causality remains unclear despite in vitro evidence that G34R directly affects Gcn5 function.
evaluation: Claims C185-C186 and C189 are supported by correlative evidence (both G34R and gcn5 mutants have reduced H3K36ac, HU sensitivity, and HR defects), and C189 is supported by in vitro data showing G34R blocks Gcn5 activity at K36. However, C190 correctly acknowledges that causality is not established, and C191 presents a speculative model for dominant effects. The inability to test causality directly (mentioned in text) limits the strength of this conclusion.

result: No evidence was found for arginine methylation of H3-G34R in fission yeast, ruling out this potential mechanism for unique G34R phenotypes.
evaluation: Claims C193-C194 are supported by mass spectrometry data (cited as Lowe et al., 2019) showing no methylation of H3-G34R. This negative result is important for ruling out one potential mechanism, though it does not explain the unique G34R phenotypes.

result: Local chromatin perturbation from mutant histone deposition is insufficient to cause IR sensitivity in the presence of wild-type H3.
evaluation: Claim C195 is supported by the observation that G34V and G34K sole copy strains are IR-sensitive (C87, C115) but mixed copy strains are not (C166). This inference about local versus global effects is reasonable given the data, though the exact mechanism remains unclear.

result: Elevated Sgo2 at ST domains in G34R/G34K mutants may delay replication timing or perturb centromere function, potentially explaining chromosome missegregation.
evaluation: Claims C200-C201 present speculative hypotheses about mechanisms linking Sgo2 accumulation to chromosome missegregation. While the correlation between Sgo2 accumulation and chromosome defects is established, these mechanistic proposals are not directly tested and remain speculative. The observation that ST silencing is maintained while chromosome missegregation is corrected in mixed copy strains (C202) complicates these models.

result: G34R and G34K mutant H3s may influence signaling through multiple phosphorylation sites on the C-terminus of H2A.
evaluation: Claim C206 is based on inference from the observation that G34R/K mutants affect Sgo2 localization (which depends on H2A phosphorylation) and previous data showing G34R affects H2A S128/129 phosphorylation kinetics (C205). While the structural proximity of H3 G34 to H2A C-terminus (C207) supports this possibility, the mechanism is not directly tested and remains speculative.

result: Previous work showed that H3-G34R mutants have reduced H3K36 trimethylation and acetylation, increased genomic instability and replicative stress, defective HR, upregulation of antisense transcripts, and enhanced subtelomeric silencing.
evaluation: Claims C1-C3 and C27-C31 reference previous work (Yadav et al., 2017) that is validated and extended by data in the current manuscript. The current study confirms these findings and provides mechanistic insights into the differences between G34R and other G34 mutations.

result: Recent work shows SETD2 activity is blocked on G34 mutant nucleosomes while NSD2 di-methylation is unaffected; differences from the current study may reflect species differences in H3 sequence or enzyme specificity.
evaluation: Claims C178-C182 discuss recent published work (Jain et al., 2020) and note discrepancies with the current study (G34W affects tri-methylation in that study but not here). The authors provide reasonable explanations for these differences (C180: fission yeast H3 differs from H3.3 at residues 28 and 31), and the observation that mixed copy strains show no global K36me3 reduction (C181) is consistent with both studies.

result: Recent work shows that H3.3 G34 mutants in mammalian cells affect transcription through Polycomb modulation, with decreased K36me3 enhancing PRC2 activity and K27me3, potentially explaining why G34 mutations occur specifically in H3.3.
evaluation: Claims C211-C215 accurately summarize recent published work (Jain et al., 2020; Martire et al., 2019) and provide context for understanding why G34 mutations are found specifically in H3.3 in cancer. These claims are appropriately cited and provide important discussion context, though they are not directly tested in the current study.
